settings.heading: A movement built in common
settings.intro: You're probably already doing your part: showing up, caring, voting, worrying about where all this is headed. What you're doing matters—and we're building a growing, open movement for everyone ready to take matters into our own hands together.

settings.heading: Common ground first
settings.text:
Left and right are constantly told they are enemies. Yet most people agree on far more than the loudest voices let us see: dignity, belonging, fair work, a livable planet, and a real say in how we live. Most people want human flourishing; they disagree on how and when.

We're optimists—not because the world is fine, and not because good intentions fix broken systems, but because humans invented these systems and humans can rewrite them.

settings.heading: One movement, many fronts
settings.text:
We're looking for actionable solutions sitting in plain sight—high-potential answers that could dramatically improve, or even solve, these problems. We create change by raising awareness of the solutions we should push for and vote for. When the obvious answers are in front of everyone, that visibility creates pressure and makes it much harder for politicians not to act. No magic fixes—let's build together:

  • Money someone can watch, freeze, or switch off. Peer-to-peer money like Bitcoin, keeping cash alive, and legal limits on surveillance and programmable money could help protect us.
  • Inflation quietly funding wars and agendas we never voted for. Money with verifiable rules nobody can print at will, like Bitcoin, could close that blank check.
  • Loneliness, rising rent, and living isolated. Co-living, shared spaces, and pooled resources could help bring community back.
  • Draining work that treats us like replaceable parts. Co-ops, local work, and tools letting small groups rival corporations could make work human-scale.
  • Tech owned by a few, shaping what we buy and think. Open source and AI as a commons could make us less dependent on its owners.
  • Showing up and still feeling powerless. Organized, peaceful collective refusal has won before. Let's learn from history.
  • Global inequality divided along borders. Open tools, money, and knowledge crossing borders could build solidarity, including with the Global South.
Use their tools for our benefit.

settings.heading: Flood the internet
settings.text:
Platforms, algorithms, and AI are routinely used to shape what we buy and what we think, and they end up dividing us along the way. We're not here to fight anyone—we're here to take those tools back and use them openly for people's benefit, using automated pipelines and social media to flood the internet with ideas worth sharing:

  • Short films: sharp, watchable animated stories about underused solutions, concentrated power, and how to push back.
  • Long-form videos and deep dives: longer pieces unpacking how these systems work and what can replace them.
  • The Journal: sourced long reads exploring money, work, community, tech, and global solidarity.

And someday, if we get the funding, we can even use targeted reach: the same precision used to sell us things, put to work for ideas worth sharing.

settings.heading: Open by default
settings.text:
Trust is earned in the open. World in Common is open source and built in public so anyone can inspect the work and take part. We publish every expense since day 0 in our transparency ledger and explain where and why we use automation in how we use AI.

We don't have all the answers, and we say so. We're learning in public alongside everyone working toward a fairer world.

settings.heading: Built with you
settings.text: A movement this big only works if we build it together. Send us personal stories, problems we should cover, video ideas, designs, or honest feedback on our contribute page. And whenever a film or post hits home, watching it to the end, liking, following, and sharing are how the message travels through the algorithms to reach the next person.

settings.heading: Revolt peacefully. Build boldly.
settings.text: If you're exhausted by broken systems running on autopilot, you're in the right place. Learn how to stop this, bring your ideas or your questions, and let's build what comes next together.
